title: Quran Study from Behrouz 16: Sura 64 and a Partial Sura 70 Study

cases.question: How did Rashad explain Quran 64:1?
cases.expected_answer_note: Rashad opens Sura 64 with the claim that everything glorifies God and that all kingship and praise belong to Him. Omnipotence is treated as the foundation for trusting God's protection, health, happiness, and fulfillment of His part when believers fulfill theirs.

cases.question: How did Quran 64 answer denial of resurrection?
cases.expected_answer_note: Quran 64:7–9 answers denial of resurrection and says every action will be accounted for. Rashad compares this with passages in which the guilty are recognized without questioning. Belief in God, His messenger, and the revealed light is presented as the path to remission and Paradise on the Day of Mutual Blaming.

cases.question: How was Hell personified?
cases.expected_answer_note: The appended Sura 70 block begins at verse 15. Hell is personified as calling those who turn away and hoard. Edip compares speaking objects across the Quran. cases.question: Which believer traits appear in Sura 70?
cases.expected_answer_note: Quran 70:22–34 lists regular prayer, a specified share for the needy, belief in judgment, reverence of punishment, chastity, trustworthy conduct, truthful testimony, and punctual prayer. The group compares the list with Sura 23 and discusses whether legally held relationships refer to captives or spouses.

cases.question: How did Rashad define chastity and marriage?
cases.expected_answer_note: Rashad expands the chastity passage into discussion of disease, social changes, marriage difficulties, arranged marriage, coercion, consent, inheritance, and temporary unions. A legitimate marriage must begin with sincere permanent intention, while deliberate temporary marriage is labeled prostitution.

cases.question: How did Rashad qualify the rich-believer statement?
cases.expected_answer_note: The post-study discussion says believers should be hard-working and explains the phrase that a rich believer can contribute more than a poor believer without denying equal belief. Rashad announces the first Quran printed as God intended and an authorized Farsi translation. He then explains that Gabriel released portions of the Quran from Muhammad's soul to memory, supplied placement instructions, and left Muhammad fully conscious while writing.
